# Funnel lab

Open `/lab/` for the experimental workshop. The original kit page and core renderer remain unchanged.

`default-configs.js` holds three seed-1234 presets. Page load and Reset variant restore that variant's complete preset, including data and print settings. The older branching export is migrated to the connected bucket tree, preserving its print settings and aggregate quantities. New sample keeps the active print settings while regenerating data.

Each variant has independent settings. On desktop, the controls sidebar scrolls independently of the figure. Shared controls adjust the chart pattern, screen pitch, hatch angle, outline weight (0.25–0.75 pt), dot gain (−80% to +20%), edge irregularity, label size, annotations, and optional paper grain. The lab uses only blue ink (`#2F4FE0`) and cool gray paper (`#E4E5E8`). Each individual pattern fills every ribbon in that variant. Atlas mix is the default for all three variants. It distributes the five available patterns across ribbons, keeping neighboring branches distinct where possible. Available patterns are dense stochastic stipple, 30% AM dots, diagonal hatch, 50% diamond lattice, and 70% coarse dots. Stipple is seeded across the entire figure rather than repeated from a small tile. Dense stipple has over twice the previous dot count; reducing dot gain makes dots smaller without reducing their number. A WebGL 2 point shader generates the seeded dots without building per-dot DOM or path commands. It keeps the full-figure distribution, six dot sizes, and independent dot-gain control. WebGL-unavailable browsers use the original six grouped vector paths. Solid ink is reserved for small marks. Older sparse stipple configurations load as dense stipple; older Atlas mix configurations retain the mix. All labels are English. Vertical is the first and default lab figure. Continuous funnels offer Half and Full mirror shapes; the mirrored form uses the same chart area, with full symmetric thickness encoding quantity. Both shapes expose curvature, height, and an optional eased fade over 0–45% of the first ribbon's left edge and last ribbon's right edge; intermediate ribbons remain fully visible. Vertical funnels open in isometric view and offer a Flat view switch. Both views share height, stage gaps, border radius (0–20 px), and terminal taper. Flat view also exposes cap curvature; its widths decrease with quantity, and adjacent rims share the same visible span even when corners are rounded. Isometric view keeps front widths proportional to stage quantities, with sparse stipple on top and screened side faces for depth. Projection depth and view rotation are adjustable. Rotating across zero reveals the opposite side while every stage follows the same tapered prism. Branching funnels expose curvature, branch spacing, and node width. The branching variant is one connected bucket tree. Each child has exactly one parent, and every non-final bucket distributes 100% of its quantity to its children, including any drop-off bucket. Node widths and adjoining ribbon widths use one common quantity scale. An optional `value` on a node asserts its quantity, including the entry total; mismatches with links are rejected. Shared destinations, multiple entry buckets, and incomplete splits are rejected with an explanation; the renderer never duplicates a bucket or resumes a disconnected aggregate. The diagram grows vertically when necessary instead of squeezing lanes together; deep graphs gain horizontal space and remain scrollable.

`config.js` generates deterministic examples and validates portable configurations. Version 3 configurations contain their version, variant, seed, all options, and complete data. Version 1 imports retain the screen migration; old opacity settings are discarded. Existing isometric configurations migrate into Vertical with isometric view selected. Older Vertical configurations without a view setting retain the flat view. Seed-generated branching examples from versions 1 and 2 regenerate as connected trees while retaining their seed and print settings. Synthetic channel activation counts are allocated within the example generator; imported custom data is never apportioned or rewritten. `lab-engine.js` renders those options without mutating the original library. New sample assigns a new seed; changing a seed regenerates its data. Applying JSON data marks the configuration as custom.

Save configuration retains a named copy in browser storage. Select it from the shelf to restore it. Export config downloads the full JSON; Import config restores that JSON with validation. Export SVG includes every ribbon, even when a path is pinned, and excludes interaction overlays. The shader screens are embedded as 3× PNGs in the SVG; the lab preview uses 2× screens. Other geometry remains vector. Mouse hover settles a thin contour over the selected section and its connected path in 150 ms; leaving takes 110 ms. A nearby pointer draws the contour along the funnel's flow direction—horizontally for continuous and branching, vertically for either Vertical view—and the contour settles onto the section on contact. The filled geometry stays stationary. Keyboard and touch feedback is immediate, and reduced-motion preferences disable all transitions and proximity movement.

Extended lab geometry options are experimental and do not yet apply to the main React component. To render a lab config programmatically in the browser:

```js
import { renderFunnel } from './lab-engine.js';
import { parseConfig } from './config.js';
const config = parseConfig(savedJson);
const svg = renderFunnel(config.data, {
  ...config.options,
  variant: config.variant,
  seed: config.seed,
  idPrefix: 'my-figure',
});
document.querySelector('#figure').replaceChildren(svg);
```

Open `/lab/benchmark.html` to compare the shader and original vector field on the same seeded figure. It reports median cold build and first-frame times over three seeds, warm reuse, dot count, and serialized SVG size, with side-by-side previews. Serve `dist/` over HTTP for development. From the repository root run `node verify-lab.mjs` to check deterministic sampling, configuration round trips, validation, and geometry at slider limits.
